entry.summary: Since 2016 travel from mainland Australia to Norfolk Island is domestic. Australian citizens need photo ID (such as a driver's licence), not a passport, though operators still recommend one.
entry.other: New Zealand and other foreign citizens need a passport and must meet mainland Australian entry rules, including any visa. Flights still use international terminals.
entry.next_check: Read the Australian Government's Norfolk Island travel information page (timed out on 31 October 2026).

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash report: Australia's rules require a report for physical currency of A$10,000 or more (or the foreign equivalent) moved into or out of Australia, with no limit on the amount carried. Bearer negotiable instruments such as cheques have no dollar threshold and must be disclosed. The page doesn't say how it applies on trips between the mainland and this external territory, so confirm with Australian Border Force.

items.text: The Commonwealth Marriage Act 1961 extends to Norfolk Island (section 8). Marriage is open to a person aged 18 or over. A person aged 16 or 17 needs an order from a judge or magistrate, given only in exceptional circumstances (section 12). A marriage valid in Australia is valid in the external territories (section 73).
